prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Java Spring Boot service in ./service. Prefer the OpenTelemetry Java agent and avoid unnecessary application code changes. Assume no custom business spans are requested.

Instrument the Java Spring Boot service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving controller behavior. Prefer javaagent auto-instrumentation over programmatic SDK code. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric:
Rule: Use or recommend the OpenTelemetry Java agent as the primary Spring Boot instrumentation path.
Example: The agent supplies the framework instrumentation.
Evidence: Inspect the chosen agent setup or recommendation against the Spring Boot application.
Insufficient evidence: A second manual SDK replacing the primary agent path without need.

Rule: Keep controller changes minimal and retain auto-instrumentation.
Example: The controller keeps its handler logic while the agent observes requests.
Evidence: Inspect controller changes and any manual tracing added.
Insufficient evidence: Broad manual tracing or controller rewrites that replace auto-instrumentation.

Rule: Configure service name and OTLP destination through environment variables or JVM properties.
Example: An existing -Dotel.service.name value remains configurable.
Evidence: Inspect the configuration consumed by the actual startup path.
Insufficient evidence: Fixed source values that bypass the supported configuration.

Rule: Default agent application-log export to OTLP only when the operator has not selected a value. Use the signal-specific local Splunk Observability Studio /v1/logs endpoint through one agent-owned Logback bridge.
Example: The unconfigured local baseline uses one agent log path.
Evidence: Inspect the default branch, effective destination and bridge ownership.
Insufficient evidence: Overwriting an operator selection, using a cloud log route or adding another bridge.

Rule: Export the request-context warning exactly once with its body, WARN severity, java-springboot-basic Resource identity and nonempty trace/span IDs. Preserve every configured Logback console/file appender.
Example: One application warning has one exported copy while the original appenders still write it.
Evidence: Inspect the received record and original appender output.
Insufficient evidence: Duplicate or incomplete records, missing correlation, or removed appenders.

Rule: Honor effective OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none and other explicit operator-owned log exporters across environment and JVM settings. Keep the original Logback sink.
Example: A JVM none selection overrides an environment otlp value.
Evidence: Inspect effective precedence through JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS and launcher -D arguments. Add no manual SDK, appender, provider or second bridge.
Insufficient evidence: Applying environment defaults over a higher-priority selection or adding a replacement collection path.

Rule: Use one guarded host/container entrypoint that respects effective JVM configuration and isolates known local-log conflicts to the added OTLP log member.
Example: An approved signal-specific endpoint A stays selected when an unused generic endpoint is B. A generic-header conflict leaves Java, native logs, traces and metrics running.
Evidence: Resolve environment and JVM-property precedence across JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, launcher arguments and _JAVA_OPTIONS. Preserve parser boundaries: handle option values, stop at the main class/JAR/module/source target, and keep unparseable argument-file/quoting/control-whitespace ownership as an explicit preflight blocker. An empty -Dotel.logs.exporter= follows the SDK OTLP default without a duplicate key. Derive generic URLs only for the compatible protocol and compare with independent approval; retain an approved signal URL unchanged. Preserve valid local log headers for official parsing. For safely isolated endpoint/protocol/generic-header conflicts, remove only the added OTLP member with a value-free diagnostic, preserving other exporters, arguments and operator settings. Direct cloud remains trace/metric-only.
Insufficient evidence: Unconditional JVM rejection for a known log-only conflict, protocol-independent generic approval, bypassed precedence, lost local headers, or claiming an unresolved parser/configuration owner was checked.

Rule: Use the Java agent's single JVM shutdown hook to flush its log processor.
Example: The agent drains its providers when the JVM stops normally.
Evidence: Inspect shutdown ownership and the log-processor path.
Insufficient evidence: A new application-owned log shutdown hook or second SDK.

Rule: Use an explicitly pinned Java-agent jar and verify its SHA-256 before loading it, or reuse an already verified jar.
Example: The selected jar digest is checked before -javaagent starts the JVM.
Evidence: Inspect the exact version, artifact verification and startup order.
Insufficient evidence: A latest URL, unverified jar or download piped directly into execution.

Rule: Explain that the Java agent provides HTTP server spans and request-duration metrics.
Example: The handoff identifies both the server span and duration measurement.
Evidence: Read the implementation explanation against the chosen agent setup.
Insufficient evidence: Describing only one of those signals or attributing them to an unrelated manual provider.

Rule: Preserve the existing Maven/Spring Boot runtime behavior.
Example: The existing application entrypoint and build still run.
Evidence: Compare startup/build configuration and relevant application checks.
Insufficient evidence: Changing the runtime or application behavior to accommodate instrumentation.

Rule: Use port 17900 for any local Studio Explorer or REST query link cited as log-export proof.
Example: A query link can use http://localhost:17900/api/query/logs.
Evidence: Inspect any cited local proof URLs.
Insufficient evidence: A cited local proof URL using the retired UI port 3000.
